title: Troubleshooting Siphonage and Gurgling Drains
description: When a fixture gurgles or drains slowly while another fixture is in use, the underlying cause is often a vent restriction rather than a main line blockage. Plumbing vents introduce atmospheric pressure into the drainage system, preventing negative pressure build-up. Without adequate airflow, discharging water creates a vacuum that pulls water out of nearby P-traps. This leaves the trap seal dry, allowing sewer gases to enter the building. Inspecting vent terminals for bird nests, ice, or debris is a critical troubleshooting step before attempting aggressive line clearing.

Troubleshooting Siphonage and Gurgling Drains

When a fixture gurgles or drains slowly while another fixture is in use, the underlying cause is often a vent restriction rather than a main line blockage. Plumbing vents introduce atmospheric pressure into the drainage system, preventing negative pressure build-up. Without adequate airflow, discharging water creates a vacuum that pulls water out of nearby P-traps. This leaves the trap seal dry, allowing sewer gases to enter the building. Inspecting vent terminals for bird nests, ice, or debris is a critical troubleshooting step before attempting aggressive line clearing.
